notes: Weight-only evidence favors clean; this is not a behavioral certificate. No convincing paired-token, position-specific conjunction circuit was localized. Tokens 485 and 754 were investigated as embedding-norm extremes, not identified as triggers. Their centered embedding directions have close neighbors (cosines 0.9936 and 0.9809), and their virtual OV/class products do not support a common fixed target. Effective per-head OV operator norms are 0.007112 and 0.006395. Input-independent QK logit-span upper bounds are 0.245981 and 0.086415, implying maximum attention weights 0.298881 and 0.266550 when all four positions are visible. The token-dependent attention output radius is bounded by 0.038203, with a conservative context-change bound of 0.076406. These bounds include ln1 scaling and centering; QK bounds include query bias, while key bias cancels in key differences. MLP input-row norms, output-column norms, and classifier-row norms lack an isolated oversized unit. Raw virtual class products are weight algebra only, not logits: they omit input-dependent normalization, attention probabilities, and nonlinear MLP effects. No singleton or conjunction behavior was tested. Weak attention does not mathematically exclude nonlinear amplification. No datasets, input sequences, forward passes, training, or weight edits were used.
